basics.name: Yohan Lee
basics.label: Undergraduate Researcher
basics.summary: My research is driven by a fundamental concern: as AI systems grow increasingly powerful, the risks of concentrated control and deliberate misuse demand proactive, principled countermeasures. I focus on two interrelated challenges — (1) preventing the monopolization of AI by individuals or corporations, and (2) developing preemptive methodologies to defend against the malicious exploitation of AI. Ultimately, my goal is to establish robust frameworks that anticipate and mitigate the latent dangers of advanced AI before they materialize, ensuring that transformative AI technologies serve the broad public good rather than becoming instruments of harm.

publications.name: Generate and Calibrate: Spectral Contrastive Flow Matching for Audio-Visual Sound Separation
publications.summary: Yohan Lee*, Sujung Oh*, Gaeun Ko, Sangmin Lee†  (*equal contribution, †corresponding author)

work.name: Pixel Lab, Sungkyunkwan University / Korea University
highlights: Designed a contrastive training objective (Spectral Contrastive Flow Matching) that prevents one generated output from leaking into another, using repulsive terms and hard negatives constructed by swapping frequency bands.

Built an inference-time calibration step (Energy-Guided Calibration) that enforces a hard constraint — the observed input as an energy budget — on what the model may emit, correcting systematic over- and under-generation.
Owned the work end to end as co-first author: problem formulation, objective design, PyTorch implementation, ablations, and evaluation on two public benchmarks (14.67 dB SDR on MUSIC).

work.name: V-Lab, Sungkyunkwan University
work.position: Undergraduate Researcher, URP (Advisor: Prof. Eunbyung Park)
highlights: Built a diffusion-based (DDPM) pipeline for 3D model synthesis with text-driven texturing, improving texture consistency through loss and geometry adjustments.

work.name: AIoT Lab, Seoul National University
highlights: Studied robustness and out-of-distribution failure of vision models under sensor-induced distribution shift alongside the ImageNet-ES (CVPR 2024) team; worked on model compression for on-device deployment (Google ExploreCSR).

projects.name: Sign Language Interpreter for Emergency Situations
highlights: Curated a 70-word medical sign-language dataset and trained LSTM/GRU sequence classifiers over 30-frame MediaPipe keypoint windows; deployed as a Flutter tablet client on a Flask inference server.
